name: Patung Dwarapala Bale Penyangra Tamu
sam3_prompt: Balinese stone guardian statue standing beside a palace pavilion
description: A Dwarapala — a guardian figure — from the Puri Agung Peliatan collection. Its name points to a role at the threshold: watching over an entrance or protected space.
history: The figure is associated with Bale Penyangra Tamu, a reception pavilion in the palace grounds. The pavilion is documented from 1825; a separate date for the statue has not been verified.
cultural_meaning: Guardian figures mark a transition. In Balinese temple architecture, a pair may stand at an entrance, symbolically protecting the sacred space beyond it.
location: Puri Agung Peliatan, Desa Peliatan, Kecamatan Ubud, Kabupaten Gianyar, Bali, Indonesia
